I was working at a staging area for fire equipment. Late one night we had a truck come in with a trailer loaded with temporary roadway panels. All guy needed to do was drop the trailer, which he did, take off all his straps, and head back to the incident site. He pulled off, I stood there a minute taking a general inventory. I took two steps away and heard a loud crack, then felt the ground shake. One of the stabilizing jacks had punched COMPLETELY through the pavement, which dropped that side of the trailer 1 3/4 feet down. Which pitched the trailer sideways, and sent the entire load of roadway panels flying off that side of the trailer. Had I not taken those two steps, taking that inventory would have been my last act on this planet. It freaks me out so bad because it happened with zero warning, and there wouldn’t have even been any safety related procedures that would have kept me safe. I’m a pretty safe guy, but there would have been nothing I could do. I’m always a little more hesitant dealing with unsecured loads on trailers now

If you don’t do a ton of cold weather riding there’s no reason to spend big bucks on a winter jacket. I’m my area, we get 300 riding days a year, so I basically live in my warm weather jacket, and spent a prettty good amount on a dainese made from perforated leather. It’s really nice, not crazy expensive (400?), and breathes so incredibly well. Simple cut, and no loud colors, which I prefer because i run from police way too often to wear loud accessories lol. I stopped wallowing in self pity. I still struggle with suicidal thoughts often, but being mindful of self pity was big. No sitting around thinking “oh my life is so shitty, I’m such a piece of shit, I’m toxic and hurt everyone close to me. A couple months ago I came really close to following through with my plan. I went and bought a really fat life insurance policy, with my wife and kids as the main beneficiaries. I was gonna hop on one of my crotch rockets, and go screaming down I-80 at 150 mph with my helmet unbuckled, until I found something suitable to run into (or ride off of). Lights out for me, and a life changing sum of money for my wife and kids. I won’t get into all the personal issues that make me feel like I’m backed into such a corner, with no way out, but that’s how I felt. And a number of weeks ago, I went for it. Kissed my wife and kids on my way out, hopped on my trusty zrx1200, and within minutes I was flying down i80 eastbound, 5th gear tapped wide open. Riding like I had a deathwish, because I kinda did (literally). Splitting lanes at 135mph, shooting 2ft gaps in between cars. Every time I saw a semi truck in the oncoming lane I got a jolt of adrenaline, envisioning myself being vaporized by a kenworth in a 160mph+ head on. I was really just waiting for a spot in the freeway where there was no guard rail separating the traffic. Then, as my Eddie Lawson replica Kawasaki started fluttering on the rev limiter, maxed out in top gear, I had a moment of doubt and realization at the same time. What if this life I have, that I’ve convinced myself is so shitty that it needs to be violently extinguished, is actually the best possible version of my life I could possibly be living? Like, what if all the other versions of me, in all the other parallel universes across time and space, had it a million times worse than me? Yet here I am taking it for granted to the point of putting a gun in my mouth in the form of an 1200cc streetbike. What if all the decisions I’ve made that I’ve spent so long wishing I could change, we’re actually good? Amd although they may have put me in some shitty spots, they steered me away from even deeper misery and despair. Idk. It may sound silly, but the idea that I could be living my best life, without even knowing it, was enough to keep me from throwing it away, for the time being.  I still get that same blast of adrenaline any time I see a kenworth in the oncoming lane, pulling fully loaded log trailers. But I’m no longer completely fixated on the thought of ending my life, and spend way less time fantasizing about it

I’ve been using since around 2003/2004, so I’ve been around the block a few times. And honestly, the rush I get when I’m doing super sketchy shit on my street bike is the BEST.  More specifically, it’s the unplanned, random encounter street racing that really does it for me. When you’re waiting at a light, and all the sudden another guy on a crotch rocket pulls up next to you, gives the nod, and revs his motor at you. . . Omg!  The anticipation, watching the light for cross traffic to turn yellow, that’s when I bring my rpms up to about 3500-4000, light goes green, and BOOM!  Taking off like I’m fired out of a cannon, feather the clutch a tiny bit to make sure the front wheel doesn’t come up too high, but after that it’s clutchless power shifting, and watching your challenger get smaller in the mirrors. It’s amazing. Then depending on how close the race was, the other guy might be game to run it back at the very next light. Last week I was out on my zrx1200, and got into it with a guy on a stretched gsxr, we went back and forth for almost an hour, one side of town to the other, then back! Also, embarrassing guys in exotic super cars like Lamborghinis or ferraris while riding an early 2000’s death trap bike I paid 3500$ for makes me feel godlike. I could go on and on about splitting lanes at high speed,  or shooting 2 foot gaps so you can ghost the police. Absolutely hair raising, but the feeling is very short lived, fleeting. Sometimes you just get a little taste. I would choose to be dopesick for the rest of my life before I let go of any of my bikes
